result.markdown: --- title: "[BetaLS]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Beta family for GAMLSS with mean-precision parameterisation. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta_ls.py#L12-L140){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python BetaLS() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} `BetaLS` extends the plain `Beta` family by letting both the mean `mu` and the precision `phi` vary smoothly with covariates, rather than treating precision as a single estimated constant. Use it for responses strictly between 0 and 1 (rates, proportions, fractions) where not only the typical level but also how tightly the response clusters around that level changes across the range of the predictors — for example, a proportion that becomes more variable in some regions of the covariate space and more tightly concentrated in others. The mean uses the logit link (as in `Beta`) and the precision uses the log link, keeping `mu` in `(0, 1)` and `phi > 0`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [None]{.doc-parameter-name} : `BetaLS` takes no constructor arguments; both `mu` and `phi` are modeled entirely through the formulas supplied to `GAMLSS`. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The two parameters use distinct link functions: $$ g_{\mu}(\mu) = \log\!\left(\frac{\mu}{1-\mu}\right), \qquad g_{\phi}(\phi) = \log(\phi). $$ If `a = mu * phi` and `b = (1 - mu) * phi`, the response follows `y ~ Beta(a, b)` with density $$ f(y \mid \mu, \phi) = \frac{y^{a-1}(1-y)^{b-1}}{B(a, b)}, \qquad a = \mu\phi,\ \ b = (1-\mu)\phi. $$ As in `Beta`, larger `phi` concentrates the distribution more tightly around `mu` (`Var(Y) = mu(1-mu) / (1+phi)`), but here `phi` is itself modeled as a smooth function of covariates rather than a single scalar. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAMLSS where both the mean and precision of a proportion response vary smoothly: ::: {#022518cd .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk from scipy.special import expit rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 300 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = expit(np.sin(x)) phi = 10.0 + 15.0 * np.abs(np.cos(x)) y = rng.beta(mu * phi, (1 - mu) * phi) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAMLSS( formulas={"mu": "y ~ s(x)", "phi": "y ~ s(x)"}, family=wk.BetaLS(), ) model.fit(data) print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAMLSS fit summary ======================================== Family: BetaLS(mu=logit, phi=log) N obs: 300 Global deviance: -548.1336 AIC: -521.9058 BIC: -473.3348 Log-likelihood: 274.0668 Converged: True (6 iterations) --- mu --- EDF total: 6.37 Smooth 1: edf = 5.37 --- phi --- EDF total: 6.74 Smooth 1: edf = 5.74 ``` ::: :::
